title: Embedding throughput & autoscaling overhaul: queueing, limits, capacity planning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Embeddings endpoints experience large bursts from crawler jobs and customers running batch vectorization which cause long queue wait times (> 700ms p95), uneven GPU utilization, and throttling incidents. Current autoscaler reacts to GPU metrics too slowly and our rate limits are coarse (per-account RPS) which forces hard rejections during short spikes. Goals: 1) keep p95 queue wait <= 200ms for hosted multi-tenant clusters; 2) achieve stable GPU utilization 60-85% across steady-state and spikes; 3) implement per-tenant soft queueing + fair-share to avoid small tenants starving; 4) provide tooling to forecast capacity and cost for committed Dedicated pods.
acceptance_criteria: p95 queue wait under 200ms on synthetic burst tests (10x baseline arrival for 30s) in staging
Autoscaler reacts within 45s to sustained surge and scales down without oscillation after 5m of reduced load
Per-tenant soft-queue implemented (priority queue + max wait TTL) with configurable SLOs exposed on console
Rate limits moved to token-bucket per-tenant + global emergency throttle; documented and visible in usage logs
Back-of-envelope capacity planner and simulation workbook that customers and SREs can run for Dedicated sizing
implementation_notes: Replace current CPU/GPU-based scaler with hybrid policy: GPU utilization + 95th p95 queue wait heuristic
Introduce an in-memory multi-priority queue with per-tenant weight; highest priority = interactive requests (console), low = bulk batch jobs
Soft-queue TTL = 5000ms default; after TTL requests are rate-limited with exponential backoff headers to client
Use a token-bucket at edge for ingress smoothing (burst size configurable per-plan), hydrate tokens from per-tenant allowance
Autoscaler config knobs: cool-down min 60s, scale-step max 3 nodes, upper-utilization threshold 82%, lower 58%
Add a simulation harness: Poisson and heavy-tailed arrivals (Pareto) with correlated bursts and diurnal patterns
Expose per-tenant queue latency and token-bucket utilization in Console; add histogram and alert at 95th percentile

benchmarks: Staging baseline: 3-node pool p95 queue wait=710ms under 5x burst (2026-02-28 replay)
Prototype: 3-node pool + soft-queue + token-bucket p95 queue wait=180ms under same replay (2026-03-11)
Target: sustain <=200ms p95 and scale within 45s for 10x sustained burst
Observed GPU util change: from 48% avg (no autoscale) to 72% avg (hybrid policy) in burst tests
risk: Medium. Changes touch edge rate-limiter, in-memory queue (stateful), and autoscaler logic. Main risks: state loss on pod restart causing unfair queue reorder, and misconfigured weight causing noisy neighbor issues. Mitigations: persist minimal queue checkpoints to Redis, add canary with traffic shadowing, gradual rollout with kill-switch feature flag.
rollout_plan: Alpha - internal canary: enable feature-flag in staging and one us-east internal pool (week 1)
Beta - 10% hosted traffic: enable soft-queue and hybrid autoscaler; monitor p95 queue and GPU util closely (week 2)
GA - gradual ramp to 100% over 2 weeks if metrics stable; for Dedicated, expose opt-in bulk pool in Console
Rollback - revert feature-flag and drain soft-queue, fallback to existing per-account hard rate-limits if p95 queue > 600ms or error rate > 0.5%
notes_for_pm: Need updated billing model for Dedicated bulk pools (separate commit for reserved capacity). PM to coordinate pricing and console copy. Also request Support playbook for customers hitting new soft-queue TTL headers.
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket edge cases (burst > allowance, token refill)
Integration tests: end-to-end request flow with simulated per-tenant weights
Load tests: stochastic arrivals including heavy-tailed bursts and correlated multi-tenant spikes
Chaos tests: pod restart during high queue pressure to validate checkpointing and resume behavior
